sense: a fuss, a scene made over something

terms.grammar: noun, first declension; plural in this sense
evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.205: tragoediās agāmus in nūgīs
Quint. 6.1.36: in parvīs lītibus tragoediās movēre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Cicero’s figure from the stage: tragoediās excitāre, movēre, to raise a great commotion; tragoediās agere, to play the tragedian. In the singular a tragedy, and also a lofty, high-flown style (Lewis & Short).

terms.register: in this sense mostly comic: Plaut., Ter.; in good prose rare (Lewis & Short)
evidence: Caecil. ap. Non. 525.4: turbam aliquam dare (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A row made by one or two people: turbās concīre (Plautus), turbam dare (Caecilius), to make a scene. Its everyday sense is a crowd (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: nunc ejusdem Appiae nōmen quantās tragoediās excitat!
phrases.english: and now what a drama the very name of the Appian Way stirs up!

phrases.latin: sī aut tragoediās agāmus in nūgīs
phrases.english: if we were to make a drama out of trifles

phrases.latin: nam Amphitruō āctūtum uxōrī turbās conciet
phrases.english: for Amphitryon will make a scene with his wife straight away
